title: Whose is it? Kenen … tämä on?
focus: Kenen means “whose”. It is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”); learn kenen as a whole.
prerequisiteSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference

exercises.prompt: Build “Whose ball is this?” Start with kenen. Use pallo (“ball”), tämä (“this”), and on (“is”).
exercises.explanation: Put Kenen before the basic noun, then tämä on. The unknown owner does not call for a personal possessive suffix.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Whose questions with kenen: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: kenen + basic singular noun + tämä + on

parts.formation: Kuka means “who”; its learned genitive form kenen asks whose thing it is.
Keep the noun in its basic singular form. Kenen is not a personal owner pronoun, so do not add a personal suffix.
Basic singular form meaning “this”.
On identifies the singular thing; the question begins with kenen rather than onko.

optionFeedback.Kenen kissa tämä on?: Recall kenen for “whose”, then place the basic noun before tämä on. Keep the noun free of a personal possessive ending.
optionFeedback.Kuka kissa tämä on?: Kuka asks who a person is; an owner question needs kenen, meaning whose.
optionFeedback.Onko kissa tämä on?: Onko asks a yes/no question; it does not ask whose the thing is.
